assumptions: SPEC-074 lightning_adapter exposes consent level and redaction version per trace; SPEC-071 reward vector stable; runtime stays standard-library only; manifest schema created by the lead under schemas/0.3.0-experimental/. Owner decisions (T001, 2026-11-14): E1-E5 accepted; balance is an equal 1:1 cap per task with no ratio parameter (OD-2); OD-1 (host usage terms) is deferred, so the terms gate ships closed and only fixtures and non-host content export. Owner decisions (T010, 2026-11-16, OD-3): another user's home path in exported bytes aborts the export (Q1 A); literal secrets not given at ingest and unknown-shape secrets are documented residual risk (Q2 A).
compatibility: Additive: new module agent_braid/lightning_export.py, CLI subcommand lightning export and an experimental manifest schema; no existing schema, contract or report changes.
domain: Braid Lightning dataset export: supervised (SFT messages JSONL) and trajectory datasets with manifests built from consented, redacted Lightning traces.
execution_contract: executionAuthorization stays false; export is offline, opens no socket, starts no process, loads no model, is not exposed through MCP, and writes only local files.
hypotheses: None; engineering specification with no scientific claim.
observation_contract: Each export records a manifest with per-record SHA-256, source task/group/rollout/attempt IDs, consent level, redaction version, ordering key, exclusion counts, canary scan result and terms decision hash.

scenarios.given: a fixture store mixing consent redacted, consent none, unconsented and unredacted traces

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes and synthetic content; rollout source only (the export input is the run store; Loom, host transcript and System One adapters are not export inputs). Consent is profile-wide, so the mix of consent states is exercised across successive profiles on one store and by unit cases, not within one read. The store fixture never yields unredacted (the adapter always redacts); only unit cases do. SPEC-074 records carry no redaction version, so the filter checks scanClean only; the dataset's redactionVersion is set by the T006 builder (procedure_005). The unreadable-file case is skipped when running as root. Overlong records are never produced (no length bound is applied); balance is procedure_007, the terms gate procedure_008, retention refusals procedure_013; writing the dataset is procedure_003 to procedure_006.
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T003 (filter part; the recorded redaction version lands with T006): lightning_export.read_runs reads each attempt of the named runs through the SPEC-074 adapter (rollout_triplets), joins task and group ids from the content-free rollout records, and yields one item per model call with its turn index and the adapter's attempt-<hmac16> pseudonym; select keeps the exportable items in order and counts every other one under exactly one reason. In a temporary store with one rollout of three model calls (full content, prompt only, no content) and consent redacted for rollout, one record is kept and two are counted content-missing; after lowering consent to none all three are consent-none; with consent redacted but only loom listed all three are no-consent. Kept plus excluded equals the model calls, also for a unit mix of every reason (unredacted included). The exclusion reasons equal the manifest schema's exclusions.required. Unit cases: a record that is not a triplet, has no redaction object, or has scanClean false or not true is unredacted; a missing prompt or response is content-missing; consent reasons win over content reasons; a gate refusal maps to its reason and an unknown one fails closed to no-consent. The raw attempt id never appears in items or selections. Refusals: a missing run (store-missing), a rollout without a rollout record and an attempt id shared by two rollouts (source-invalid), a run named twice (invalid-argument), and an unreadable events file, a malformed JSON line, a non-object content line, a symlinked events file and a malformed salt (each Run refused with a lowercase code) are all ExportError with a fixed text naming no id or path, no chained cause and suppressed context; an adapter refusal is Adapter refused a source with its code, or source-invalid when its code is not a lowercase code. Negative controls: classifying from the triplet's losses alone fails the no-consent test; the T003 module before the review fixes fails the shared-attempt, run-twice, adapter-refusal and four of the five damaged-store cases.

obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T004: lightning_export.supervised writes one JSONL line per unit, trace_adapter.canonical_bytes(record) plus a newline (ASCII, a non-ASCII turn escaped), {recordId, messages} (plus outcome with outcome_field), and a manifest record entry whose sha256 is the line's SHA-256 and which validates against the manifest schema's record item. scenarios.given: a three-turn rollout with and without token IDs

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes and synthetic rollout content. The token-ID path is exercised only with token IDs added to items in the test: no SPEC-074 triplet carries them. The comparison of lines with a written manifest is procedure_005 and procedure_006, balance procedure_007, and the canary scan procedure_010. Transition records carry the attempt's reward vector, not a per-call reward. Trajectory records keep only the attempt's exported calls, so an excluded middle call leaves a gap inside turnRange (declared text-level-merge, never a token-ID merge). The writers share one loop (_write) with the supervised writer, whose limits follow the same rule. The terms gate refuses host-model output without an owner record (procedure_008).
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T005: lightning_export.rollout_records writes {recordId, rolloutId, attemptId (pseudonym), turns [{prompt, response, toolCalls}], reward, status} as trace_adapter.canonical_bytes plus a newline, with a manifest record entry whose sha256 is the line's SHA-256 and which validates against the schema's record item. A three-call succeeded rollout (one non-ASCII call, one with a tool call) yields three transition records with turnRange [0,0], [1,1], [2,2] and no limits, each carrying the attempt's SPEC-071 reward vector unchanged and status succeeded, and one trajectory record with three turns, turnRange [0, 2], outcome success and limit text-level-merge (adapter triplets carry no token IDs). With token IDs on every turn of consecutive calls forming a prefix chain the trajectory declares no limit; a broken chain, a turn without token IDs, a non-integer token ID, or a chain whose middle call was excluded (turnRange [0, 2] with two turns) gives text-level-merge; token IDs never enter a record. A one-call failed rollout merges nothing and carries status failed. A rollout with two attempts is refused by read_runs with source-invalid and a fixed text. Order is E3 (task before rollout: a rollout id that sorts first but belongs to a later task comes last) and independent of input order. The T004 checks apply: host-model items refuse with terms-gate-missing at both levels, unselected items with invalid-argument, an unknown level with invalid-argument, and a written record outside the shape (tool calls not a list) with invalid-record. check_rollout refuses an unknown key, a raw attempt id, no turns, an unknown turn key, non-text turn text, tool calls that are not a list, a non-object reward or one with other keys, an unknown status and a malformed record id. No raw attempt id reaches a line or entry. Negative controls (mutants, each fails a test): token-ID merge ignored, the limit never declared, the prefix check dropped, the consecutive-call check dropped, the one-attempt check dropped, check_rollout removed, the input and terms check removed, the reward dropped.

scenarios.given: a task with 5 successes and 2 failures

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes and synthetic fixture content; one seed per assertion plus a range of seeds to show the seed matters, not a statistical test of the choice. Same data and seed give the same selection (the key holds no salt-dependent pseudonym; a rollout has one attempt, which read_runs enforces). The balance unit is the attempt, so a long attempt and a short one weigh the same. No claim is made that balance benefits a model (E4). The terms gate refuses host-model output without an owner record (procedure_008).
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T007: lightning_export.balance_equal keeps, per task, min(successes, failures) attempts of each outcome by the lowest SHA-256 of [seed, taskId, runId, rolloutId] (no attempt pseudonym, so a re-ingest with a new salt selects the same attempts). Fixture store: task-a with 5 successes (one of two calls), 2 failures and 1 attempt without a reward; task-b with 3 successes only; task-c with one of each; task-d with 2 successes and 5 failures. With seed 0 task-a keeps 2 + 2, reported as successes 5, failures 2, unknown 1, keptPerOutcome 2, dropped 4; task-d keeps 2 + 2, reported successes 2, failures 5, keptPerOutcome 2, dropped 3; task-b keeps nothing and is reported singleOutcome true, keptPerOutcome 0, dropped 3, not padded; task-c keeps one of each. The kept rollouts for seed 0 are pinned (task-a ro-a0, ro-a4, ro-f0, ro-f1; task-d ro-d0, ro-d1, ro-e2, ro-e4) and the rank of one key is pinned to its hex; a second store with the same data and another salt (disjoint attempt pseudonyms) selects the same rollouts. Attempts are kept whole and kept plus dropped model calls equal the input. The choice is the same for reversed input and reruns with the same seed (identical records bytes and digest), changes with the seed, and the manifest records the seed. Rollout exports balance by default at both levels and validate against the schema; dropped attempts leave neither their pseudonym nor their rollout id in records.jsonl or manifest.json; balance none exports every attempt with an empty report. check_manifest, through export_dataset with a tampered balancer, refuses (invalid-manifest, nothing written) a 1-vs-1 task claiming keptPerOutcome 5 and dropped 0, a cap below the minimum, a wrong singleOutcome, a wrong dropped count, an extra or a missing kept attempt, an empty report under balance equal, a report under balance none, a duplicate task and a kept task missing from the report. Supervised exports are never balanced: balance equal is refused (invalid-argument) with or without the outcome field, and the default supervised export has balance none, an empty report and no balance exclusions. A ratio, unknown or boolean balance and a negative, boolean, fractional or text seed are refused (OD-2: no ratio parameter); an export that balance empties refuses with no-records. The terms gate stays closed: host-model runs refuse with terms-gate-missing, also when balance would drop them. Negative controls (mutants, each fails a test): max or the failure count instead of min, a reversed rank, a rank without the task or with the attempt pseudonym, an unseeded rank, the terms check after balance, unknown attempts kept, dropped calls not counted, a none default, the supervised guard removed, singleOutcome never set, and each report check removed.

obtained_evidence.limits: Synthetic records only: no real provider's terms were reviewed (OD-1 deferred) and nothing here says any provider permits training; host-run units come from synthetic fixtures. Coverage is by exact model id from the attempt_start event; units without one cannot be covered. The record's provider name is informational, not checked against the host; binding is by host plus exact model id. Host and model come from the ingested trace data (rollout record, attempt_start event) and are not independently attested. One record covers one host per export. Privacy is checked for the owner's uid and mode bits only (no ACLs). Expiry is the owner's validUntil date compared with the export's UTC day; no review period is set by Agent Braid.
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T008: load_terms_decision reads terms/<name>.json under the plugin home's lightning directory and the export refuses every non-fixture unit not covered by it with terms-gate-missing before writing anything, with a text naming no path or field value and no chained cause. scenarios.given: a fixture with a planted canary that survived redaction

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes and synthetic canaries. The scan catches known shapes only: as the SPEC-074 privacy review says, pattern-based redaction cannot catch every secret shape or every piece of personal data (for example names in free text). Not detected, by owner decision OD-3 Q2 A: a literal secret the store was not given at ingest, free text of unknown shape, a raw attempt id typed inside content, and encodings nested twice or more; canaryScan clean means no hit for the listed classes, not free of secrets. The home-path check refuses any /Users/<name> or /home/<name> path not inside a longer segment, so a trace that mentions any such path (for example /home/runner/ on CI when it is not the current $HOME, /srv/home/x or a URL path /api/users/42) blocks the export until the run is cleaned or purged. obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes, synthetic runs and an injected clock. Retention is per run (content lines are never older than their run); the export refuses at the exact expiry instant while the SPEC-074 sweep removes the run one instant later. A missing profile refuses (the sweep would default to 30 days), the intended fail-closed choice. The index is read by lightning purge's output; an entry, with its absolute output path and run ids, stays while its dataset exists, also after its runs are purged, and is pruned by a purge apply once the dataset is deleted or changed. Datasets written before T013, copied or moved are not listed; the listing names local paths of the owner's own datasets; lightning sweep and purge --expired do not list datasets. The owner approved on 2026-11-16 the additive purge output (citingDatasets, datasetsNote) in lightning_cli.py; SPEC-074's spec, store, adapter, redactor and config are unchanged.
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T013: the manifest records, per cited run, the profile's traces.retentionDays and the UTC date of the instant the run expires (createdAt plus that many days). The export refuses a run from that exact instant, one instant before the SPEC-074 sweep removes it (stricter on purpose, fail closed); the comparison is in epoch seconds. With one fresh run and one created 40 days earlier, the old run's record is excluded and counted as retention-expired, the manifest cites only the fresh run, and its content is not written; exporting only the old run refuses with retention-expired and writes nothing. Boundaries on the 30-day default: expiry tomorrow and one second before the instant export; at the instant (which the sweep still keeps), one second after and a day later refuse; a profile with retentionDays 1 refuses a day after creation and exports a second before. Runs created at 23:59:59Z and 00:00:00Z show expiry dates of the next and the following day and refuse exactly one day after creation, a second earlier exporting. A profile without a valid bound (retentionDays 0) and no profile refuse with retention-expired. The four boundary results are the same with TZ set to UTC, Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Pago_Pago and Asia/Kolkata (TZ restored by addCleanup). Each real export first writes a private index entry atomically (temporary file in the same directory, then rename; directory 0700, file 0600; keys schema, out, digest, runIds; no content); a dry run writes none, a failed dataset write removes it, an interrupt at the rename leaves neither the entry nor its temporary file, and a leftover temporary file is not listed. lightning purge --run-id and --all, preview and apply, list in citingDatasets each indexed dataset whose manifest still exists, matches its digest and cites a purged run, with a note that purge does not delete datasets; a run no dataset cites lists none; the dataset directory is byte-identical before and after preview and apply; an export between preview and apply does not stale the preview; deleted, changed, relative, symlinked, dotted, trailing-slash, wrong-directory and non-string entries are not listed; apply prunes the index entries of deleted and changed datasets and keeps their files, a preview prunes nothing. The SPEC-074 purge and retention tests still pass unchanged. lightning export --help states that expired records are retention-expired, that datasets are outside purge and that the index remains until the dataset is deleted. Negative controls (mutants, each fails a test): the injected clock ignored, an inclusive or a one-day-late boundary, the check skipped, the expiry of another run used, the expiry day computed in local time, a fixed 30-day bound, the no-bound check removed, no refusal when every record expired, no index entry, uncited datasets listed, a changed manifest accepted, the entry kept after a failed write, purge listing nothing, a non-atomic index write, the temporary file kept, pruning on preview, never pruning, a non-canonical out accepted, purge writing into a dataset and pruning that deletes dataset files. Two mutants are equivalent and survive: dropping the absolute-path test (the canonical-path comparison also rejects a relative out) and dropping the canonical check of out (the check of manifest.json rejects a symbolic link on its path).
